claim: A meta-analysis restricted to follow-up >24 months in mesial TLE found seizure freedom of 72.5% [65.6-78.5%] after temporal lobe resection vs 57.1% [51.2-62.7%] after MRgLITT (P<0.01), with more minor (transient) complications after resection.

bibliographic_record.authors: Ekman FR, Bjellvi J, Ljunggren S, Malmgren K, Nilsson D
bibliographic_record.title: Laser Interstitial Thermal Therapy versus Open Surgery for Mesial Temporal Lobe Epilepsy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

supporting_passage: For seizure freedom, TLR was superior, with 72.5% [65.6%, 78.5%] of patients achieving postoperative seizure freedom compared to 57.1% [51.2%, 62.7%] for MRgLITT (P value <0.01).
passage_location: Abstract (unstructured). Abstract only (full text not read). Europe PMC REST API (resultType=core, abstractText) for PMID 39332763; https://europepmc.org/abstract/MED/39332763; accessed 2026-11-01

population_and_design.design: systematic review and meta-analysis (pooled proportions per arm; mostly non-comparative/observational studies -- study count and n not_reported in abstract)

endpoint.reported_endpoint: postoperative seizure freedom at follow-up >24 months
endpoint.protocol_mapping_v1: seizure freedom -> favourable (definition, e.g. Engel I vs IA, to_verify)

reported_observation: TLR 72.5% vs LITT 57.1% seizure freedom at >24 months; minor complications more frequent with TLR.
author_inference: TLR provides superior seizure freedom but increased risk of transient complications.
contradictions: Pichardo-Rojas 2026 found no significant LITT vs open difference in propensity-matched studies (RR 0.85, p=0.30) and in TLE studies (RR 0.88, p=0.34); Ekman compares pooled single-arm proportions, which is more confounded by patient selection.
overlap_note: Pools published LITT and resection series; overlaps with other meta-analyses in this family (to_verify which primary studies).
